answer: Persistent work-credit ledger. Each identity’s credit equals verified useful work minus consumed services, and credit is nontransferable. New identities start at zero and must fund queries via slow accumulation or pay a cold-start surcharge. Cloning N identities costs N surcharges plus N parallel work streams, so honest single-identity operation stays cheaper. Like a fable, the rule is simple; like a glacier, credit accrues slowly; each river of service draws it down.
